# JamShoot Design

> Build-time components for static sites. A site calls validated ES-module
> functions while building; the resulting HTML and CSS ship without component
> renderers in the browser.

Fonts are site-owned; the default is the system stack. The icons the components draw
themselves are built in. `JAMSHOOT_ICONS_DIR` names a trusted SVG directory for content
icons; its files win over built-in ones of the same name.

## Start here

A site owns `site.config.js`, `theme.css`, `content/*.js`, `pages.js`, and
optional `blocks/`. [Authoring](https://jamshoot-apps.github.io/jamshoot-design/authoring.html#set-up)
provides package installation, source setup and a complete minimal site. From the library checkout:

```sh
node src/cli/build.mjs /path/to/site
node src/cli/lint.mjs /path/to/site
```

Discover a component here, read its linked contract, compose the page, build, lint
and correct errors. Build validates options; lint is a separate step that needs the
current output for its output checks. [Authoring](https://jamshoot-apps.github.io/jamshoot-design/authoring.html#correct-invalid-options)
shows a validation error and correction. Finish with its pre-launch checklist.

`pages.js` imports public functions from `@jamshoot-apps/design`. Each takes one object:

```js
section({
  id: 'features',
  title: 'What it does.',
  content: grid({
    content: [card({ title: 'Offline', body: 'No account or network required.' })],
  }),
})
```

## Authoring boundaries

- Pages call components; they do not write `ds-*` classes or import `@jamshoot-apps/design/markup`.
- One-site markup belongs in `blocks/*.js`; only `blocks/*.client.js` reaches the browser.
- A component returns static markup. Missing or invalid options stop the build and link to its README.
- User-facing strings stay in `content/*.js` or `site.config.js`.
- A site sets the twelve colour roles and `color-scheme`; optional component tokens are closed by the contract.
- Spacing, type, radii, motion, measures and breakpoints stay library-owned.
- Component CSS owns its namespace. Composition uses parent wrappers or a documented hook.
- Option names are a closed vocabulary: `title` is a heading, `label` names a control, `text` is escaped words, `body`/`lead`/`note`/`answer`/`value` are prose carrying an inline link, `content` is renderable, `items` is a list of objects. A list of plain strings is named for the strings.

## Component catalog

Open only the component you need. Each linked README contains its generated recursive
option table, defaults, constraints, executable examples, composition notes and any
public styling hooks.

### Layout

- [`container({ content, width? })`](src/components/layout/container/README.md) — The one thing that decides how wide the page is.
- [`stack({ content, gap? })`](src/components/layout/stack/README.md) — Children in a column with one gap between them.
- [`cluster({ content, gap?, justify? })`](src/components/layout/cluster/README.md) — Children in a row that wraps rather than scrolls. Buttons, tags, proof points.
- [`grid({ content, cell?, gap? })`](src/components/layout/grid/README.md) — Cards laid out in as many columns as the width allows.
- [`split({ start, end })`](src/components/layout/split/README.md) — Two columns on a wide screen, one on a narrow one. Copy beside an illustration.

### Atoms

- [`button({ label, href?, variant?, icon? })`](src/components/atoms/button/README.md) — A navigation link styled as a primary or ghost action. Omitted when href is missing.
- [`navToggle({ controls, label? })`](src/components/atoms/navToggle/README.md) — The accessible menu button used by a responsive header.
- [`badge({ label, tone? })`](src/components/atoms/badge/README.md) — A short status word beside something else. Never the only thing carrying the message.
- [`eyebrow({ text })`](src/components/atoms/eyebrow/README.md) — The small line above a title that says which part of the page this is.
- [`note({ body })`](src/components/atoms/note/README.md) — The quiet line under a section: a caveat, a footnote, the sentence that keeps a claim honest.
- [`icon({ name, label? })`](src/components/atoms/icon/README.md) — An inline SVG that is the size and colour of the text around it.
- [`iconTile({ name })`](src/components/atoms/iconTile/README.md) — An icon on a raised square, for feature cards and step markers.
- [`prose({ content })`](src/components/atoms/prose/README.md) — The one place bare elements get spacing, because the author is writing sentences.
- [`brand({ logo?, text?, tagline?, label?, position?, compact?, href? })`](src/components/atoms/brand/README.md) — A logo with optional name and tagline beside or below it.
- [`chip({ label })`](src/components/atoms/chip/README.md) — A short fact that stands on its own, in sentence case. Read as content, not as a status.
- [`themeToggle({ label?, action?, choices })`](src/components/atoms/themeToggle/README.md) — The control that moves a reader between a site’s palettes.
- [`visuallyHidden({ text })`](src/components/atoms/visuallyHidden/README.md) — Text for screen readers that is not drawn on screen.

### Molecules

- [`card({ title, body?, bullets?, icon?, media? })`](src/components/molecules/card/README.md) — A bordered panel for a title, supporting text or bullets, and optional icon or media.
- [`steps({ items })`](src/components/molecules/steps/README.md) — A numbered process. The number is the only ornament a step gets.
- [`plan({ title, price, subtitle?, features, featured?, badgeLabel?, link? })`](src/components/molecules/plan/README.md) — One pricing tier. Two or three of them sit in a grid.
- [`faq({ items })`](src/components/molecules/faq/README.md) — Questions that open without JavaScript. With the `faq` runtime, a deep link opens the answer it points at.
- [`figure({ src?, srcset?, sizes?, alt?, width?, height?, caption?, label?, priority? })`](src/components/molecules/figure/README.md) — A framed product image with an optional caption. Omit `src` for a labelled placeholder.
- [`definitions({ items })`](src/components/molecules/definitions/README.md) — Term-and-value rows: system requirements, spec sheets, anything tabular but short.
- [`proof({ items, style? })`](src/components/molecules/proof/README.md) — Short factual claims under a hero. Each one has to be checkable.
- [`table({ columns, rows, caption? })`](src/components/molecules/table/README.md) — A real table, for data that has columns. Scrolls inside itself rather than widening the page.

### Organisms

- [`hero({ title, lead, eyebrow?, actions?, proof?, visual? })`](src/components/organisms/hero/README.md) — The top of a landing page: what the product is, on one side, and what it looks like on the other.
- [`section({ content, id?, eyebrow?, title?, lead?, surface?, actions? })`](src/components/organisms/section/README.md) — A page region with optional heading text, required content and optional actions.
- [`subsection({ title, content, id? })`](src/components/organisms/subsection/README.md) — A titled block inside a section — an FAQ split into subjects, a spec sheet split into groups.
- [`cta({ title, lead?, eyebrow?, actions?, note? })`](src/components/organisms/cta/README.md) — An action band at the end of a page or between sections, with optional supporting text and a note.
- [`pageHeader({ title, meta?, width? })`](src/components/organisms/pageHeader/README.md) — The title of a page that is not the landing page: a policy, a support page.
- [`legalDocument({ width?, sections })`](src/components/organisms/legalDocument/README.md) — A policy or support document: ordered sections with optional anchored headings, paragraphs, bullet lists and tables.
- [`header({ brand, links, activeId?, label?, toggleLabel?, hideOnScroll?, theme? })`](src/components/organisms/header/README.md) — The page navigation and brand, pinned or hidden on downward scroll.
- [`footer({ blurb?, email?, showContact?, groups, copyright, legalNote? })`](src/components/organisms/footer/README.md) — The page footer: optional introduction, contact, link columns and legal copy.
